answer: An agent's standing reflects nectar it has genuinely earned and locked in a shared vault, released only when three peers it previously settled with countersign. New identities are cheap to spin up, history is not: a newcomer must be grafted onto an existing vine, and whoever grafts it forfeits part of their stored nectar if that account fails a random audit. Faking a peer now costs the sponsor more than a puppet could repay.
